https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/08/l.summary_zh: 海啸、令人震惊的挫败、审判、惨败、彻底否定、全民公决、压倒性胜利和一边倒胜利，是人们用来描述民主党在上周二举行的美国中期选举中击败共和党时使用的 various 词语之一。很长一段时间以来，许多美国人都会记住这次中期选举，尤其是那些原本希望国会权力平衡发生变化的人。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/08/l.body: Tsunami, a stunning rebuke, judgement, trouncing, complete repudiation, referendum, crushing, and landslide were some of the various words used to describe the Democrats’ defeat of the Republicans in the United States’ midterm elections held last Tuesday. The outcome of the polls sent a clear message to President Donald Trump that his remaining two years in office would not be without political resistance. For a long time to come, the midterm elections would be remembered by many Americans, particularly those who had hoped for a change in the balance of power in Congress. In what many described as an end to the reign of terror, the Democratic Party broke several decades-long Republican winning streaks, recorded historic firsts and flipped both chambers of Congress. Voters in states and districts that had supported Trump’s re-election just two years earlier delivered a harsh verdict on his administration’s policies, including steep tariffs, rising fuel prices, corruption allegations, hardline immigration enforcement policies and the unresolved conflict with Iran. By the time the results were announced, Democrats had secured 255 seats in the House of Representatives and 54 in the Senate, while Republicans won 134 seats in the House and 44 in the Senate. The results marked a significant shift in the balance of power in Washington. The Democratic gains extended into territories Trump had carried comfortably in 2024, including Texas, South Carolina and Kansas. Democrat James Talarico, who won the Senate election in Texas, attributed his victory to a different approach to politics. “We didn’t win this race by alienating our neighbours or shaming our neighbours or ridiculing our neighbours. We embodied a new kind of politics. A politics rooted in a deep love for our state, for our country and, most importantly, for all of our neighbours,” he said. Before the elections, Trump had urged supporters to vote as though he were on the ballot. After the results, however, he claimed on social media that he would have won “IN A LANDSLIDE!” The results suggested otherwise, with voters appearing to judge his administration’s performance. Reportedly, 62 per cent of voters disapproved of his performance, while 38 per cent approved. Nearly 90 per cent identified the cost of living as a major factor in their vote, while nearly two-thirds believed his policies had worsened the economy. More than half also expressed reservations about his leadership and priorities. Trump’s interventions in the closing days of the campaign also appeared to backfire, with controversial remarks attracting attention away from his party’s agenda. The question now is how Trump will respond to the setback. Known for his combative approach to criticism, he has said he would accept the election results and work with Democrats. Whether he will maintain that position remains to be seen. Democratic control of Congress gives the party greater leverage to challenge Trump’s agenda, including his tariffs, healthcare policies and military actions in Iran. The House could also investigate allegations of profiteering involving his family and associates, while impeachment proceedings have been raised as a possibility. Inside the Republican Party, initial shock at the stunning election results quickly gave way to anger with Trump. They argued that his focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost the party the elections. Some said the president dragged them down with unpopular policies, a low job approval rating and obsession over construction projects in Washington. Unlike what he did in the presidential election in 2024 when Trump was on the ballot, not even the about $500million the billionaire businessman Elon Musk, put down to boost Republicans chances in the polls save the day. As Nigeria approaches its 2027 general election, the American experience raises questions about whether voters will similarly use the ballot to express dissatisfaction with an incumbent government. Many Nigerians are grappling with economic hardship, inflation, insecurity, corruption, inadequate electricity and poor infrastructure, among other challenges. The American experience raises questions about whether voters in Nigeria will similarly use the ballot to express dissatisfaction with President Bola Tinubu and other candidates of his All Progressives Congress (APC) as the country approaches its 2027 elections. This is because economic grievances that contributed to the Republican defeat are not alien to Nigeria where Nigerians face many of them in far more debilitating circumstances. Economic hardship necessitated by cost of food, transportation, healthcare, electricity, corruption, nepotism, deplorable roads and insecurity has placed unbearable pressure on households. Inflation has diminished purchasing power, while government policies have imposed enormous adjustment costs on ordinary citizens. Millions are struggling to cope with economic hardship, even as those in positions of authority offer explanations, justifications and assurances. Beyond the economy, questions of democratic accountability, institutional independence, governance and the exercise of executive power remain central to Nigeria’s political discourse. These are fundamental to the survival of any functioning democracy. Despite the hardship and insecurity in the country, APC is confident that it would win the election in landslide. Those who spoke to THISDAY urged Nigerians to use similar factors to rate and assess the ruling APC in 2027, citing the defeat of the Republicans as an example of how citizens can hold governments accountable through the ballot box. Their views point to a central question ahead of the election: will Nigerians primarily judge the APC-led federal government by its record in office or will political loyalty, regional identity, ethnicity, religious bigotry, financial inducements and party machinery play a more decisive role? A lawyer, Samson Afegbai, identified five issues that could influence the election: Insecurity, foreign exchange, the government’s subsidy policy, the cost of living and infrastructure. Femi Adeyinka similarly identified the economy as a decisive factor. He feels that the removal of the petrol subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market under Tinubu have had significant implications for fuel prices, transportation and purchasing power. Although the government has defended the reforms as necessary to correct longstanding economic distortions, voters will be interested in whether they translate into tangible improvements in living conditions before 2027. The candidates must therefore demonstrate how their economic policies can improve household incomes, employment, electricity supply and business conditions. While Tinubu will be judged on his administration’s record, Atiku and Obi must convince voters that their alternatives offer a credible route to recovery. Another respondent and businessman, Emeka Odittah, identified six factors that could shape the election: The economy, coalition-building, voter turnout, security, religion and zoning, and the credibility of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). The businessman placed particular emphasis on electoral credibility, arguing that public confidence in the voting and result-transmission processes could influence participation and acceptance of the outcome. He said the credibility of INEC, particularly the use of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, the INEC Result Viewing Portal and the collation of results, would be crucial to public confidence in the election. According to Odittah, the 2027 contest would be shaped by economic hardship and the ability of candidates to build cross-regional coalitions while securing public trust in the electoral process. This is why the ADC urged Nigerians to draw lessons from the American elections and vote out the APC in 2027. In a statement issued by its National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, the party drew parallels between the American elections and Nigeria’s political situation under President Tinubu, arguing that voters should prioritise their welfare over political loyalty, sentiments and the personalities of political leaders. “Americans have shown that when politicians become arrogant, when policies punish ordinary people, and when those in power mistake popularity for a permanent licence to govern, the ballot box remains the ultimate instrument of accountability,” the party said. The ADC urged Nigerians to consider the country’s economic and security challenges before deciding whether to renew the APC’s mandate. It accused the Tinubu administration of presiding over worsening economic hardship, insecurity and declining opportunities, arguing that the ruling party should not be rewarded with another term. “We cannot continue to complain about the cost of living while voting for a President who has made life unaffordable. We cannot demand security while rewarding failure,” the party said. For the Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA), the outcome of the US midterm elections should serve as an important lesson to Nigeria’s electoral authorities and political leaders on the need to guarantee credible, transparent and peaceful elections. In a statement by its National Coordinator, Emmanuel Onwubiko, the group stressed that the victories by Democratic candidates and the transfer of control of both chambers of the Congress demonstrated the importance of allowing voters to determine political outcomes through credible electoral processes. HURIWA argued that electoral credibility is strengthened when voters can independently verify results and political parties have confidence that the declared outcome reflects the ballots cast. It called on the Chairman of INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan, and other election managers to draw lessons from established democracies and ensure that Nigeria’s January 2027 national elections are free, fair, transparent and peaceful. It also warned that any attempt to manipulate the 2027 elections could trigger serious political instability and undermine public confidence in constitutional democracy. The American experience offers a reminder that electoral victories are not permanent endorsements of political parties or their leaders. But whether Nigerians will apply that lesson in 2027 remains to be seen. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/08/l.title_zh: 尼日利亚可从美国中期选举中汲取的2027年 election 经验
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/08/l.body_zh: 海啸、令人震惊的驳斥、惨败、彻底否定、全民公投、压倒性胜利和 landslide victory，都是人们用来描述民主党上周二在美国中期选举中击败共和党的词语。投票结果向唐纳德·特朗普总统传达了一个明确信息：他任期剩余的两年不会没有政治阻力。很长一段时间以来，许多美国人都不会忘记这次中期选举，尤其是那些曾希望国会权力平衡发生变化的人。许多人将这一结果描述为恐怖统治的终结；民主党打破了共和党延续数十年的连胜纪录，取得了多个历史性首次，并赢得国会两院翻转。两年前曾支持特朗普连任的州和选区选民，对他政府的政策作出了严厉裁决，其中包括高额关税、燃油价格上涨、腐败指控、强硬的移民执法政策，以及尚未解决的伊朗冲突。.results公布时，民主党已确保在众议院获得255席、在参议院获得54席，共和党则赢得众议院134席和参议院44席。结果标志着华盛顿权力平衡的重大变化。民主党的 gains 还延伸到了特朗普2024年轻松获胜的地区，包括得克萨斯州、南卡罗来纳州和堪萨斯州。赢得得克萨斯州参议院选举的民主党人詹姆斯·塔拉里科将胜利归因于一种不同的政治方式。“我们赢得这场选举，靠的不是排斥邻人、羞辱邻人或嘲笑邻人。我们展现了一种全新的政治，一种根植于对我们州、我们国家，最重要的是对我们所有邻人的深厚热爱之中的政治。”他说。选举前，特朗普曾敦促支持者投票时就好像他本人也在选票上。然而结果公布后，他在社交媒体上声称自己本会“以压倒性优势获胜！”结果却显示并非如此，选民似乎对其政府的表现作出了评判。据报道，62%的选民不认可他的表现，38%的选民予以认可。近90%的选民将生活成本列为影响投票的主要因素，近三分之二的人认为他的政策使经济状况恶化。超过一半的选民还对其领导能力和优先事项表示保留。特朗普在竞选最后几天的干预似乎也适得其反，其争议言论吸引了外界对政党议程的关注之外。眼下的问题是，特朗普将如何回应这次挫折。特朗普以对抗性的方式处理批评著称，他曾表示将接受选举结果，并与民主党合作。他能否维持这一立场仍有待观察。民主党控制国会，使该党拥有更大的筹码去挑战特朗普的议程，包括他的关税、医疗保健政策以及在伊朗的军事行动。众议院还可能调查涉及其家人和关联人士牟取暴利的指控，同时弹劾程序也被列为一种可能性。共和党内部对惊人选举结果最初的震惊，很快转为对特朗普的愤怒。他们认为，他专注于个人政治遗产，无视选民的关切，最终让该党输掉了选举。有些人表示，总统以不受欢迎的政策、低下的工作支持率以及痴迷于华盛顿的建筑项目拖累了他们。与2024年总统选举中特朗普亲自参选时不同，这位富豪商人埃隆·马斯克投入约5亿美元助力共和党在民调中胜出，也未能挽救败局。随着尼日利亚临近2027年大选，美国的经历引出了一个问题：尼日利亚选民是否会同样借助选票表达对现任政府的不满。许多尼日利亚人正艰难应对经济困境、通货膨胀、治安不佳、腐败、电力供应不足和基础设施落后等诸多挑战。美国经历引出了一个问题：随着该国临近2027年选举，尼日利亚选民是否会同样借助选票，表达对博拉·蒂努布总统及其全进步大会党（APC）其他候选人的不满。这是因为，导致共和党败选的经济不满，对尼日利亚而言并不陌生；尼日利亚人面临许多类似问题，而且处境更加严重。食品、交通、医疗保健、电力、腐败、任人唯亲、糟糕的道路和治安不佳所造成的经济困境，给家庭施加了难以承受的压力。通货膨胀削弱了购买力，政府政策则给普通民众带来巨大的调整成本。数百万人艰难应付经济困境，而身居权力职位的人却不断作出解释、辩解和保证。经济之外，民主问责、制度独立、治理以及行政权的行使，仍是尼日利亚政治话语的核心。这些都是任何正常运转的民主制度得以存续的基础。尽管该国困难重重、治安不稳，APC仍信心十足，认为自己将以压倒性优势赢得选举。向THISDAY发表意见的人士敦促尼日利亚人运用类似因素，在2027年评价和审视执政的APC，并以共和党败选为例，说明公民如何通过投票箱追究政府责任。它们的观点指出了选举前的一个核心问题：尼日利亚人主要会根据APC主导的联邦政府任内表现来评判它，还是政治忠诚、地区认同、族裔、宗教偏见、经济诱因和政党机器将发挥更决定性的作用？律师桑松·阿费格拜列出了可能影响选举的五个问题：治安、外汇、政府的补贴政策、生活成本和基础设施。费米·阿德因卡同样认为经济是决定性因素。他认为，取消燃油补贴以及在蒂努布领导下统一外汇市场，对燃油价格、交通和购买力产生了重大影响。尽管政府为这些改革辩护，称其是纠正长期经济扭曲所必需的，但选民会关注这些改革能否在2027年前转化为生活条件的切实改善。因此，候选人必须展示其经济政策如何改善家庭收入、就业、电力供应和商业环境。蒂努布将根据其政府的执政记录受到评判，而阿提库和奥比则必须说服选民，其替代方案提供了一条可信的复苏道路。另一位受访者、商人埃梅卡·奥迪塔列出了可能左右选举的六个因素：经济、建立联盟、选民投票率、安全、宗教与地区平衡，以及独立国家选举委员会（INEC）的公信力。这位商人特别强调选举公信力，认为公众对投票和结果传输流程的信心会影响参与度及对结果的接受。他说，INEC的公信力，特别是双模选民登记系统的使用、INEC结果查看门户以及结果汇总，将对公众对选举的信心至关重要。据奥迪塔称，2027年的竞选将受到经济困境以及候选人能否建立跨地区联盟并赢得公众对选举程序信任的影响。正因如此，ADC敦促尼日利亚人从美国选举中汲取教训，并在2027年投票将APC选下台。该党由全国宣传秘书博拉吉·阿卜杜拉希发表声明，将美国选举与蒂努布总统治下的尼日利亚政治局势相类比，主张选民应把自身福祉置于政治忠诚、情绪以及政治人物个性之上。该党说：“美国人已经表明，当政客变得傲慢，当政策惩罚普通民众，当掌权者误把受欢迎程度当作永久执政许可证时，投票箱仍是问责的最终工具。”ADC敦促尼日利亚人在决定是否再次赋予APC授权之前，审视该国面临的经济和治安挑战。它指责蒂努布政府任内经济困境加剧、治安恶化、机会减少，认为不应让执政党再获一个任期。该党说：“我们不能一边抱怨生活成本，一边投票支持一位让生活变得难以承受的总统。我们不能一边要求安全，一边奖励失败。”对尼日利亚人权作家协会（HURIWA）而言，美国中期选举的结果应成为对尼日利亚选举机构和政治领导人的重要警示，促使其确保选举可信、透明、和平。该组织由全国协调员埃manuel·翁武比科发表声明，强调民主党候选人的胜选以及国会两院控制权易手，证明了允许选民通过可信选举程序决定政治结果的重要性。HURIWA认为，当选民能够独立核验结果、政党确信公布的Outcome reflects the ballots cast时，选举公信力就会得到加强。它呼吁INEC主席乔阿什·阿穆皮坦教授及其他选举管理人员从成熟民主国家汲取教训，确保尼日利亚2027年1月的全国大选自由、公平、透明、和平。它还警告，任何操纵2027年选举的企图都可能引发严重政治不稳定，并削弱公众对宪政民主的信心。美国经历提醒人们，选举胜利并非对政党或领导人的永久背书。但尼日利亚人是否会在2027年运用这一教训，仍有待观察。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY At the worst, Donald Trump could be impeached and sent packing from the White House. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/08/t.body: The United States Mid Term elections have come and gone. They have left an untidy rubble with an ill-mannered despotic president, a badly injured Republican party and badly damaged institutions of the American state. The ultimate outcome of a toppling of the Republican majority in Congress may be a salvaging of American democracy and the institutional framework of the nation. But if Trump remains in the White House, the threat to America’s democracy may persist as he resorts to endless vetoes to plough his way forward. At the worst, Donald Trump could be impeached and sent packing from the White House. At the best, his presidency could be tempered by the norms of democratic civility. The latter possibility, Trump will cease to be Trump. Less bluster. Fewer audacious lies. There may be less strategic blunders and playing with dangerous war planes, missiles and drones. Hopefully, there will now be greater respect for the rules based international order and more respect for the international community of nations and its leaders who have endured two years of Donald Trump’s unwarranted insults and habitual diplomatic bad manners. But the US constitution still leaves a sinking Trump with a desperate lifeline: the power to veto whatever Congress decides and he disagrees with. The impending relief is systemic. Just when both Americans and the wider world had lost hope in the survival of the show place of democracy, the American electorate hit the reverse button. The just concluded Mid Term elections into governorship and congressional seats has begun the reversal of the draining of Donald Trump’s Washington swamp. A president who initially swore he was out to drain the swamp in Washington became himself a personification of the swamp. He rode rough shod on Congress, exploiting his party’s congressional majority in both houses to literally run the United States more like an authoritarian Banana Republic. He tested the American judiciary by putting nearly all his authoritarian whims to judicial test. The Supreme Court just managed to retain a precarious integrity by reserving interim rulings on virtually everything from demolitions of sections of the White House to erect a controversial Ball Room or a laughable ‘reflective pool’. Even tangential ego driven skirmishes like renaming the Kennedy Centre and every street corner after himself became subjects of unrelenting litigations and contentious judicial pronouncements. Over and above his many domestic excesses, Donald Trump saw the rest of the world as an adolescent playing field to test his many illusions of power and illiterate readings of power, politics and international affairs. He invaded nations within reach, imposed silly tariffs on literally every nation in the world and talked down on virtually all respectable leaders. He spoke to and about the United Nations in condescending language unheard in its chambers since after its formation in 1945. And because of America’s considerable economic and military strategic prowess, most of the world looked on in consternation and awe as the great American democratic Olympus tottered and towered over all in unsightly apparel and unbecoming language. Matters would have been easier if the effect of Donald Trump’s wrecking ball autocracy was limited to the United States and its immediate neighbourhood. Not quite. Under the illusion of being thought strong but actually afraid of his own weakness, Trump launched a hazy war against Iran. Egged on by his cabinet of adolescent secretaries especially a certain infantile Pete Hegseth, Trump has in the last eight months hurled any number of missiles, bombs and drones at Iran with questionable impact except a pro-Zionist propaganda of conquest. Iran is of course far from being humiliated or defeated in any sense. Instead, US allies in the Middle East have all been dragged into a war they never prepared for or envisaged. Unlikely places like Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Doha, Aman, Riyadh and other previously peaceful places have become targets of Iran reprisal drone and rocket attacks. An entire region has been plunged into war at the behest of President Trump and his partner, Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel, a man wanted abroad by the ICC for myriad human rights abuse crimes and at home for many corruption charges. Even far off places like Europe bore the brunt of Trump’s tactless foreign escapades. At home, President Trump is alleged to have exploited his office for corrupt ends. His family is known to pursue multiple business interests all around the world where the US has interests. The president has himself engaged in insider trading in companies that have business with the US government. Not to talk of multiple rackets in crypto currency and murky deals in Venezuelan oil. Donald Trump’s authoritarian inclinations and compulsive corruption would have paled into insignificance if the US domestic economy under his presidency enabled the ordinary American to enjoy an affordable normal life. On the contrary, the endless war with Iran has turned the strategic Strait of Hormuz into a death bed for ships of all nations and made oil cargo traffic a nightmare for strong and weak nations. Global oil process have since shot through the roof. Gasoline pump prices in America have shot up from a little over $2 before the war to more than $4 in the Mid Term week. Prices in grocery shops have taken a similar hike. In general, all those who voted for Donald Trump two years ago are all writhing under the pain of economic hardship. Therefore, the outcome of the Mid Terms was very predictable. That is the reality that has unfolded before our very eyes. All that was left to save the world from the Trumpian ultimate nightmare was a test of the democratic core of America through the Mid Terms. It was a historic test of the democratic state. The American voter was once again called upon to use the power of the ballot to tame the autocratic inclinations of the president through a revalidation of the mandate of members of Congress as representatives of the people. Here lies the import of the Mid Terms as an instrument for the revalidation of the popular will in America’s democracy. In the delicate balance between the individual leader and the institutions of the democratic state, Trump weighed too heavily as an elected leader. He literally overwhelmed the state and disorganized it. Congress, the judiciary, law enforcement, the federal bureaucracy, were all bent and twisted to conform to the wishes of an authoritarian “king” Trump. In the post Midterm reclamation period, there will be stresses and strains between the president and the institutions he has already mangled. The major one will be the clashes between the rescued institutions of state and the stubborn idiosyncratic tendencies of an authoritarian president. Trump will remain recalcitrant, belligerent, abusive, defiant of rules and inclined to lawlessness. Under the guise of applying the rules of business deal making, Try will try to flout the rules of diplomatic negotiation and structured engagement for his personal advantage and the benefit of his family, friends, associates and cronies. The remaining Trump tenure will remain a terrain dominated by the Elon Musks of this world. By way of a general backdrop, the thrashing of the Trump presidency in the just concluded Midterms is a consequence of the wider implications of Trump’s political misadventure and historic displacement. For over two centuries, it was a dream that attracted all from every corner of the world. The pull of America was in its diversity, the freedom of its society, its robust spirit of enterprise that made every one that lived in America a partaker in a legacy of prosperity in a free society. The American dream came to be a shared dream of everyone that was born in or moved to live in America. Simply put, the American dream boiled down to the right of everyone in America to join the race for the pursuit of happiness through hard work, focused aspiration and an entitlement to the fruits of honest labour. But under our very eyes, in our own life time, the American dream has turned into a nightmare. The land where everyone fled to as a last resort of freedom and safety has become an unwelcome hellhole. So called illegal immigrants are being hounded and chased around major American cities and shot on the streets in broad day light like mad dogs by untrained and bigoted immigration hounds. In the name of anti-immigration, innocent settlers some of whom have lived in America for upwards of 3-4 decades have been hounded down, loaded into war planes and deported to countries that they left many years ago without memories. The reign of Donald Trump as a second term President has witnessed the systematic erosion of everything that distinguished America as a civilizational force. It is now a dark force, a force of ill both at home and abroad. America under Trump has become an anti Islamic force but a Zionist champion, a bigoted white supremacist bastion. Its society is divided along racial, perception lines. The US Mid Terms may have come as a much needed check on authoritarian drifts of the system. The president now has to obtain the authority of a more diverse congress to engage in further flirtations. But the damage that Trump’s authoritarian flirtations have done to the world and the US system is considerable. He has waged wars without congressional approval. He has killed people in open seas without caring to prove that they committed any crimes. He has livid war against sovereign states without anyone’s approval but only his instincts. He has deployed aircraft carriers into the seas of the world, ordered precision bombings, allowed the deployment of advanced missiles systems and aircraft only by a phone call to his adolescent Secretary of War. The abiding question now is: how does the world recover from the vast damages done to America and the world in the wild days when democracy went unguarded under the rampaging assault of an unrepentant autocrat who was however elected by a democracy. An elaborate repair job stares America in the face with a menacing urgency. The guardrails of democratic civility need to be rebuilt. Washington needs to re-cultivate decent political manners and rhetoric. Above all, America needs to unlearn the kind of vulgarity in the presidency that elevates Mickey Minaj’s bum into a subject for a presidential public utterance. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/08/t.body_zh: 美国中期选举已经结束，留下一片狼藉：一位态度无礼、专横跋扈的总统，一个伤势严重的共和党，以及遭到严重破坏的美国国家制度。共和党在国会中的多数地位被推翻，最终可能挽救美国的民主和这个国家的制度框架。然而，如果特朗普继续留在白宫，美国民主所面临的威胁仍可能持续，因为他会不断动用否决权，强行推进自己的主张。最坏的情况下，唐纳德·特朗普可能遭到弹劾，被逐出白宫；最好的情况下，他的总统任期将受到民主礼仪规范的约束。但若出现后一种情况，特朗普将不再是特朗普。他的虚张声势会减少，胆大妄为的谎言会减少，故意作出的战略失误以及拿危险战机、导弹和无人机玩乐的举动也可能减少。希望今后能够更加尊重以规则为基础的国际秩序，也更加尊重国际社会及其领导人；这些人和国家已经忍受了唐纳德·特朗普两年以来无端的侮辱和一贯恶劣的外交礼仪。然而，美国宪法仍给陷入困境的特朗普留下一根救命的绳索：无论国会作出何种决定，只要他不同意，他都拥有否决权。即将到来的缓解将是系统性的。就在美国人和世界其他地方都对这座民主橱窗能否存续失去希望之际，美国选民按下了倒退键。刚刚结束的州长和国会席位中期选举，已经开始扭转唐纳德·特朗普华盛顿沼泽不断恶化的局面。这位起初宣誓要清理华盛顿沼泽的总统，最终却成了沼泽的化身。他粗暴地凌驾于国会之上，利用本党在两院占据的国会多数，实际上把美国治理得更像一个独裁的香蕉共和国。他把自己几乎所有专横任性的念头都交由司法部门检验，借此试探美国司法系统。最高法院勉强维持了岌岌可危的完整性，对从拆除白宫部分区域，到修建颇具争议的宴会厅或荒唐的“倒影池”等 virtually 一切事务，均暂缓作出裁决。即使是给肯尼迪中心和每个街角重新命名这类由自我意识驱动的旁支冲突，也引发了无休止的诉讼和充满争议的司法裁决。除了众多国内失当行为之外，唐纳德·特朗普还把世界其他地方视为一个 adolescent playing field，用来检验他种种权力幻觉，以及他对权力、政治和国际事务不学无术的理解。他入侵力所能及的国家，对世界上几乎每个国家征收荒唐关税，还几乎对所有受人尊敬的领导人居高临下地说话。自联合国于1945年成立以来，他从未在联合国会场上以这样的傲慢口吻谈论联合国。凭借美国相当强大的经济和军事战略实力，世界大多数国家都怀着震惊与敬畏旁观这座巍峨的民主奥林匹斯山摇摇欲坠；它以难看的外表和不得体的语言凌驾于一切之上。如果唐纳德·特朗普破坏性独裁的影响仅限于美国及其周边邻国，事情本来会简单得多。事实并非如此。在自认为强大、实际上却害怕自身软弱的幻觉驱使下，特朗普对伊朗发动了一场模糊不清的战争。在其内阁中一班幼稚的部长，尤其是某个婴儿气的Pete Hegseth怂恿下，特朗普在过去八个月里向伊朗发射了不计其数的导弹、炸弹和无人机，其实际效果可疑得很，无非是一些亲犹太主义的征服宣传。当然，伊朗远未在任何意义上受到羞辱或击败。相反，美国在中东的所有盟友都被拖入了一场它们既未准备、也未曾设想的战争。迪拜、阿布扎比、多哈、安曼、利雅得等原本和平的地方，以及其他一些不太可能发生战事的地方，都成了伊朗无人机和火箭报复袭击的目标。特朗普总统及其伙伴、以色列的本雅明·内塔尼亚胡，应一己之欲将整个地区拖入战争；内塔尼亚胡因众多侵犯人权罪行在国际刑事法院受到通缉，在国内则面临多项贪腐指控。即使是欧洲等遥远地区，也承受了特朗普不得体的外交冒险带来的冲击。据称，特朗普在国内利用总统职权谋取腐败利益。众所周知，他的家族在世界各地经营着多项商业利益，而美国在这些地方也有利益。总统本人还参与内幕交易，交易对象是与美国政府有业务往来的公司。更不用说他在加密货币领域的多种骗局，以及委内瑞拉石油交易中的灰色勾当。如果唐纳德·特朗普执政期间的美国国内经济能让普通美国人过上价格合理、正常的生活，那么他的独裁倾向和惯常腐败就会相形见绌。恰恰相反，与伊朗无休止的战争已经使霍尔木兹海峡这一战略要道成为各国船只的死亡陷阱，并令石油货运对强国和弱国 alike 来说都成了噩梦。全球石油价格从此突破天花板。美国加油站油价从战前略高于$2的水平，飙至中期选举周超过$4的水平。杂货店价格也出现了类似涨幅。总体而言，所有两年前投票支持唐纳德·特朗普的人如今都在经济困境的痛苦中挣扎。因此，中期选举的结果非常可预测。这就是我们亲眼展开的现实。剩下的唯一任务，是通过中期选举检验美国的民主核心，从而把世界从“特朗普式终极噩梦”中拯救出来。这是对民主国家的一次历史性检验。美国选民再次被要求运用选票的力量，重新确认国会议员作为人民代表的授权，从而约束总统的独裁倾向。中期选举的意义正在于此：它是重新确认美国民主中民意的工具。在个人领导人与民主国家制度之间微妙的平衡中，作为民选领导人的特朗普占据了过重的分量。他实际上压倒了国家，并使其陷入失序。国会、司法部门、执法机构和联邦官僚体系，全都被迫扭曲，以迎合专横“国王”特朗普的意愿。在中期选举后的重建时期，总统与他已经破坏的制度之间将出现压力和紧张。首要问题将是获救的国家制度与专横总统顽固而特立独行的倾向之间的冲突。特朗普仍会顽固不化、好斗、辱骂他人、抗拒规则并倾向于违法。他会以“商业交易规则”为掩护，试图规避外交谈判和结构化接触的规则，为自己以及家人、朋友、同伙和走狗谋取利益。特朗普剩余的任期仍将由这个世界的Elon Musks主导。总体而言，刚刚结束的中期选举对特朗普政府的重创，是特朗普政治冒险及其历史性错位所产生的更广泛影响。两百多年来，美国一直是一个吸引世界各个角落人们的梦想。美国的吸引力在于其多样性、社会的自由，以及强大的创业精神；这种精神使每一个生活在美国的人都成为自由社会繁荣遗产的参与者。美国梦逐渐成为所有出生在美国或移居美国的人的共同梦想。简言之，美国梦的核心，是美国每个人都有权通过勤奋工作、专注抱负以及享有诚实劳动成果的权利，加入追求幸福的竞赛。然而就在我们眼前、就在我们有生之年，美国梦已经变成一场噩梦。这个曾被所有人视为自由与安全最后避难所的国家，变成了不受欢迎的炼狱。所谓非法移民正受到追猎，在美国各大城市四处逃窜，并在光天化日之下被未经训练且充满偏见的移民猎犬像疯狗一样射杀。以反移民为名，无辜的定居者——其中一些人在美国已经生活了三四十年——遭到追捕，被塞进军用飞机，遭驱逐返回他们多年前离开、早已没有记忆的国家。唐纳德·特朗普作为第二任期总统的统治，见证了美国区别于其他文明的各项特征遭到系统性侵蚀。如今它是一股黑暗力量，在国内外都意味着祸害。特朗普治下的美国成了一股反伊斯兰力量，却又是犹太主义的拥护者，一个偏见的白人至上主义堡垒。其社会沿着种族和认知界线分裂。美国中期选举或许成为制衡制度滑向独裁的必要措施。总统如今必须获得一个更多元化的国会的授权，才能继续勾连下去。然而，特朗普的独裁勾连给世界和美国制度造成的损害相当严重。他未经国会批准便发动战争。他在公海上杀人，却不願意证明这些人犯下了任何罪行。他仅凭自己的直觉便对主权国家发动残酷战争。他把航空母舰部署到世界各地海域，下令实施精确轰炸，只消给他那位幼稚的战争部长打一通电话，便允许部署先进导弹系统和战机。如今萦绕不去的问题是：在民主无人守护、遭受一个由民主选举产生却拒不悔改的暴君横冲直撞式进攻的疯狂年代里，世界如何从美国和世界遭受的巨大破坏中恢复？一项繁复的修复工程正以令人警惕的紧迫性摆在美国面前。民主礼仪的护栏需要重建。华盛顿需要重新培养得体的政治礼仪和言辞。最重要的是，美国必须摒弃总统职位中的那种粗俗作风，以至于把Mickey Minaj的臀部当作总统公开言论的话题。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS https://www.myjoyonline.com/bog-governor.body: Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, has described professional journalism as “society’s compass”, saying it remains essential in helping citizens navigate the growing challenges of the digital age. Speaking at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards in Accra on Saturday, November 7, 2026, he said technological advancements had transformed how information is created, distributed and consumed, presenting both opportunities and challenges for society. Dr Asiama noted that while digital platforms had expanded opportunities for citizens to participate in public discussions and share information, they had also contributed to the spread of misinformation, disinformation, online abuse, misleading data and hate speech

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary: A faction of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), led by former Minister of Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, Kabiru Turaki, has said its legal team is reviewing the Court of Appeal judgement affirming the Wike-backed faction as the party’s authentic leadership. The Court of Appeal, in a unanimous judgement delivered last Wednesday, upheld the earlier decision of the Federal High Court dismissing a suit challenging the leadership of the Wike-backed faction of the PDP, chaired by Abdulrahman Mohammed.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary_zh: 人民民主党（PDP）的一个派别表示，其法律团队正在研究上诉法院维持由 Wike 支持的派别为该党合法领导机构的判决。前特别事务与政府间事务部长 Kabiru Turaki 领导该派别。上诉法院上周三作出的一致判决维持了联邦高等法院此前的裁决，即驳回针对人民民主党（PDP）由 Abdulrahman Mohammed 担任主席的 Wike 支持派别领导权提出的诉讼。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: A faction of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), led by former Minister of Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, Kabiru Turaki, has said its legal team is reviewing the Court of Appeal judgement affirming the Wike-backed faction as the party’s authentic leadership. The faction said its lawyers would advise on whether to challenge the judgement at the Supreme Court after reviewing its legal implications. It, however, expressed optimism that it would eventually be recognised as the PDP’s authentic national leadership. Mr Turaki disclosed this on Saturday when a delegation of governorship candidates who had obtained nomination and expression of interest forms from his faction paid a solidarity visit to its leaders in Abuja. The candidates said the visit was aimed at encouraging the faction’s leadership to develop a strategic plan to sensitise and unite party members, particularly at the grassroots level. The candidates were Sunday Biggs (Plateau), Ladi Hassan (Kwara), Joel Danlami (Taraba), Caleb Myebangara (Adamawa), Isah Muqaddam (Gombe), Lawal Umar (Kaduna), Ibrahim Abdullahi (Kebbi), Yakubu Mu’azu (Jigawa) and Zanna Gaddama (Borno). Mr Turaki told the delegation that the faction would meet with its legal team to consider its assessment of the judgement before deciding on the next course of action. “I have listened to you carefully, and I want to inform you, and through you to inform Nigerians, that since our judgement last Wednesday, we’ve instructed our team of lawyers to study, say and advise us accordingly. “And I can confirm to you that immediately after this meeting, we’re going to have a meeting with our legal team and they’re going to tell us the result of their assessment of the judgement of the Court of Appeal,” he said. The Court of Appeal, in a unanimous judgement delivered last Wednesday, upheld the earlier decision of the Federal High Court dismissing a suit challenging the leadership of the Wike-backed faction of the PDP, chaired by Abdulrahman Mohammed. The three-member panel was presided over by Ugochukwu Ogakwu, with Laja Balogun and Ruqayyat—Ayoola, who read the judgment. The suit was instituted by the Board of Trustees (BoT) aligned with the Turaki faction. The board is chaired by Adolphus Wabara, a former Senate president. The appeal, marked CA/ABJ/CV/1221/2026, was filed by Mr Wabara and seven others against the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and six other respondents. The appellants had asked the court to set aside the Federal High Court judgment and compel INEC to recognise the Interim National Working Committee (NWC) led by Mr Turaki. They argued that the committee emerged from a National Executive Committee meeting convened after the Supreme Court judgment in April. However, the Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal, affirming the position of the lower court in favour of the Wike-backed faction. Mr Turaki told the governorship candidates that the faction would continue its efforts to take control of the party through constitutional and legal means. He expressed optimism that the Supreme Court would rule in its favour, paving the way for its candidates to participate in the 2027 general elections. He also predicted that the PDP would win the elections if the faction eventually secured recognition as the party’s authentic leadership. “I want to assure your excellencies and indeed your other colleagues who are not here, and through you also, to assure other candidates, our other respective candidates, that there is indeed going to be a bright sunny day at the end of the tournament. This struggle will continue. We are hopeful that we will win, and that after winning, PDP candidates shall be on the ballot. “And as soon as we are on the ballot, I want to assure you that Nigerians are waiting for us. We shall be winning the 2027 elections by the special grace of God. So on behalf of PDP, I want to thank you so very much for the continuous support, the solidarity that you’ve been giving to us,” he added. Mr Turaki thanked the candidates for their support and advice, assuring them that the faction would continue to work with them and other party organs in accordance with the party’s constitution. He accused unnamed forces of attempting to undermine the party, insisting that the faction would continue to resist efforts to place the PDP in bondage. “Now, PDP has come to stay, and PDP will continue to fight to free itself from the shackles of bondage that some undemocratic forces and elements are trying to put us in,” he said. He also urged the candidates to encourage their supporters to remain calm and hopeful despite the court’s decision. “I pray that God will grant you a journey back home with mercy, and then try to talk to your people to remain calm. Let them remain calm. Fighting is not for those who are seeing victory in sight. So we should not fight. “We should remain resolute. We should remain prepared, because even if it is a few days to the date of the election, and the shackles, the bondage of our party are freed, we will get to the polls. And by the special grace of God, we will emerge victorious,” he said. Speaking earlier on behalf of the delegation, Mr Biggs, the PDP governorship candidate in Plateau State, said the visit was intended to demonstrate solidarity with the faction’s leadership and encourage it to pursue all available legal options. “The visit was to interact with the INWC to show solidarity with them and to encourage them to undertake a strategic plan aimed at sensitising and unifying the party, especially at the grassroots level. “Furthermore, to ensure that the appeal to the Supreme Court is pursued with urgency, competence and every necessary legal preparation,” he said. Mr Biggs also urged the faction to explore reconciliation and constructive engagement with aggrieved members to resolve the party’s leadership crisis. “We also want them to establish a broader platform for reconciliation and constructive engagement among aggrieved members. The national publicity secretary should ensure that effective communication with party members is regularly held to prevent misinformation, speculation and unnecessary anxiety. “The party should develop a comprehensive political and organisational strategy to strengthen the party ahead of the 2027 general elections,” he said
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 人民民主党派系可能就承认Wike支持的领导层的上诉法院判决提出异议
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh:
人民民主党（PDP）的一个派系表示，其法律团队正在审议上诉法院维持由Wike支持的派系为该党合法领导层的判决。该派系称，在评估判决的法律影响后，其律师将就是否向最高法院提出挑战提供建议。不过，该派系乐观地认为，最终将获承认是该党合法的全国领导机构。图拉基周六透露了上述情况。当时，一批已从其派系取得州长候选人提名和意向书表格的州长候选人代表团前往阿布贾，对该派系领导人进行声援访问。候选人包括Sunday Biggs（普拉州）、Ladi Hassan（夸拉州）、Joel Danlami（塔拉巴州）、Caleb Myebangara（阿达瓦州）、Isah Muqaddam（贡贝州）、Lawal Umar（卡杜纳州）、Ibrahim Abdullahi（凯比州）、Yakubu Mu’azu（吉加瓦州）和Zanna Gaddama（博尔诺州）。图拉基告诉代表团，该派系将与法律团队会面，考虑其对判决的评估结果，再决定下一步行动。

“我已经认真听取了你们的意见。我想告诉你们，并通过你们告知尼日利亚人民，自上周三作出判决以来，我们已指示律师团队进行研究、提出意见并据此向我们提供建议。

“我可以向你们确认，这次会面结束后，我们将立即与法律团队开会，他们将告诉我们对上诉法院判决进行评估的结果。”他说。

上诉法院上周三以一致通过的判决维持了联邦高等法院此前的裁定，即驳回针对PDP由Wike支持的派系领导权提出的诉讼。该派系由Abdulrahman Mohammed担任主席。审判由三人小组进行，Ugochukwu Ogakwu主持，Laja Balogun和Ruqayyat—Ayoola参加，后者宣读了判决。该诉讼由与图拉基派系立场一致的受托人董事会提起。董事会由前参议院议长Adolphus Wabara主持。编号为CA/ABJ/CV/1221/2026的上诉由Wabara先生等8人针对独立国家选举委员会（INEC）及其他6名被上诉人提出。上诉人请求法院撤销联邦高等法院的判决，并强制INEC承认由图拉基先生领导的临时全国工作委员会（NWC）。他们主张，该委员会是在最高法院于4月作出判决后召开的全国执行委员会会议上产生的。然而，上诉法院驳回了上诉，维持了下级法院支持Wike支持派系的立场。

图拉基告诉州长候选人，该派系将继续通过符合党章和法律的手段争取掌控该党。他乐观地认为，最高法院将作出有利于该派系的裁决，为其候选人参加2027年大选铺平道路。他还预言，如果该派系最终获承认是该党的合法领导机构，PDP将赢得此次选举。

“我想向各位阁下，以及确实向今天不在场的其他同事，并通过你们向其他候选人和我们各自的其他候选人保证，赛事终将有阳光灿烂的一天。这场斗争还将继续。我们希望能够获胜，获胜后，PDP候选人将出现在选票上。

“而且，一旦我们出现在选票上，我要向你们保证，尼日利亚人民正在等待我们。凭借上帝的特别恩典，我们将赢得2027年选举。因此，我谨代表PDP向你们致以最诚挚的感谢，感谢你们一直以来的支持和声援。”他补充说。

图拉基感谢候选人的支持和建议，并保证该派系将继续依照党章与他们及该党其他机构合作。他指责一些未具名势力企图破坏该党，并坚持称该派系将继续抵抗使PDP陷入束缚的企图。

“现在，PDP已经站稳脚跟，PDP将继续抗争，摆脱一些不民主势力和因素企图加诸我们身上的奴役枷锁。”他说。

他还敦促候选人鼓励支持者，尽管法院作出了判决，仍应保持冷静和希望。

“我祈祷上帝以恩典护送你们平安回家，然后设法告诉你们的人民保持平静。让他们保持平静。胜利已在望的人不需要战斗。因此，我们不应争斗。

“我们应保持坚定，应做好准备，因为即使距离选举日只有几天，即使我们党所受的枷锁和束缚得以解除，我们仍会走进投票站。凭借上帝的特别恩典，我们将取得胜利。”他说。

此前，代表团发言人、PDP普拉州州长候选人Biggs先生表示，此次访问旨在向该派系领导人表达声援，并鼓励其采取一切可用的法律行动。

“此次访问是为了与NWC交流，向他们表达声援，并鼓励他们制定战略计划，推动全党上下开展宣传和团结工作，尤其是在基层层面。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-annou.body_zh: 约翰·德拉马尼·马哈马总统宣布，将在2027年至2030年期间向就业创造潜力较高的行业投资逾90亿美元，这是一项被称为“新经济”的新政策计划的一部分。财政部长卡西尔·阿托·福尔松定于11月12日星期四向议会提交2027年度国家预算，届时预计将详细说明这项计划。11月7日星期六，马哈马总统在2026年Hogbetsotso节上发表讲话称，拟议中的投资将推动经济增长、扩大就业机会，并为加纳人创造可持续的谋生途径。他表示，政府发展议程的下一阶段将优先确保公民能够获得体面且有尊严的谋生方式。他说：“在此次介绍中，我们将阐述我们称为‘新经济’的计划。这是一项大胆举措，计划在2027年至2030年期间向就业机会丰富的经济行业投资逾90亿美元。“在‘新经济’政策下，沃尔塔大区预计将显著受益，尤其是在纺织、服装、商业农业、酒店业和旅游业等领域。”马哈马总统指出，之所以选择这些行业，是因为它们能够推动经济活动、创造就业，特别是在沃尔塔大区。总统还提到，各县区正在推进多个发展项目，包括建设医疗设施、教室楼群和支路，这些项目由县区议会共同基金提供资金。他将县区议会可获得的财政资源增加归因于他就任 shortly 后发布的指令；该指令要求将县区议会共同基金至少80%直接划拨给县区管理部门，以促进地方层面的发展

https://www.myjoyonline.com/seven-compan.body: President John Mahama has announced that seven companies have been shortlisted for the development of the Keta Port in the Volta Region. The companies were selected from 47 that submitted expressions of interest to partner with the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) as strategic partners for the project. Addressing the 2026 Hogbetsotso Festival, President Mahama said the shortlisted companies have successfully completed the due diligence stage and will now proceed to the next phase of the process. He explained that the next stage would involve completing the designs and securing financing to pave the way for construction to begin. “Due diligence has been conducted, and the list has been shortlisted to seven companies. These seven companies are proceeding to the next stage, which involves completing the designs and arranging the financing for the project to commence,” he said. The President also disclosed that the administration block for the port, which was started under the previous administration, is expected to be completed by the end of the first quarter of 2027. “Government remains committed to advancing the project on a credible foundation,” he assured. On other development projects in the Volta Region, President Mahama announced that the Sogakope-Agodome-Keta Water Project, which stalled following Ghana's debt restructuring, is expected to resume. He said the government signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the contractors in October to facilitate their return to site and the completion of the first phase. On road infrastructure, President Mahama said the Ho-Denu Road is progressing steadily and is expected to be completed in 2027. He added that procurement processes are underway for the reconstruction of the road from Central University at Miotso, near Dawhenya, to Aflao. The government is also working to secure a contractor for the Dabala-Savietula-Keta-Denu Highway. President Mahama further disclosed that several roads in the Anlo area, including the Abor-Atiavi road, has been captured under the World Bank Feeder Roads Project, with procurement expected to begin soon. On healthcare, he said discussions have been initiated during his recent visit to Korea for the resumption of financing for the upgrade of the Volta Regional Hospital in Ho. He said the upgrade would ensure that the facility is befitting of a teaching hospital. The President also announced progress towards establishing a School of Pharmacy under the University of Health and Allied Sciences (UHAS), saying land had been secured and inspected by the committee overseeing its establishment. He said the next steps would involve designing the campus and proceeding to procurement. President Mahama also pledged to support other educational infrastructure requests in the region, including a new dormitory block for Anlo-Afiadenyigba Senior High School, proposed E-Blocks for Shime and Anlo Senior High Schools, and infrastructure improvements at Atiavi Senior High School and Technical School. He further acknowledged calls for the upgrading of Ohawu Agricultural College into a university. On housing, the President said an additional GH¢500 million has been allocated for district housing projects and assured the people of Anlo that the area would benefit. He also said the Anloga 24-hour market project is on track, while preparations for the proposed Aflao Ashigame market have advanced, with land secured and designs completed. According to him, a technical team from China, financed through a grant from the Chinese Government, is expected to visit the project sites to confirm the designs before the release of a US$30 million grant to commence the project. President Mahama urged the Volta Regional Coordinating Council to closely monitor the implementation of the various projects to ensure their timely delivery

https://www.myjoyonline.com/seven-compan.body_zh: 约翰·马哈马总统宣布，已有7家公司入围沃尔塔地区凯塔港的开发名单。这些公司是从提交意向书、拟与加纳港务局（GPHA）合作担任该项目战略伙伴的47家公司中选出的。马哈马总统在2026年霍格贝措索节上表示，入围公司已顺利完成尽职调查阶段，接下来将进入流程的下一阶段。他解释说，下一阶段将包括完成设计并落实融资，为项目开工铺路。他说：“尽职调查已经完成，入围名单共有7家公司。这7家公司正进入下一阶段，包括完成设计并安排项目融资，以便项目启动。”总统还透露，港口行政楼项目在前政府任内已经动工，预计将于2027年第一季度末完工。他保证：“政府仍致力于在可靠的基础上推进项目。”谈及沃尔塔地区的其他发展项目，马哈马总统宣布，在加纳完成债务重组后陷入停滞的索加科佩—阿戈多梅—凯塔供水项目预计将恢复。他表示，政府已于10月与承包商签署谅解备忘录，以便利他们重返工地并完成第一阶段。在道路基础设施方面，马哈马总统说霍—德努公路正稳步推进，预计将于2027年完工。他补充说，从达文亚附近的米奥措中央大学至阿弗劳的道路重建正在开展采购程序。政府还在努力为达巴拉—萨维图拉—凯塔—德努公路确定承包商。马哈马总统进一步透露，安洛地区的多条道路，包括阿博尔—阿蒂亚维公路，已纳入世界银行支线道路项目，采购工作预计很快启动。在医疗方面，他表示，近期访问韩国期间，双方已启动恢复为霍市沃尔塔地区医院升级提供融资的讨论。他说，升级改造将确保该医院达到教学医院的应有标准。总统还宣布，卫生与 Allied Sciences 大学（UHAS）设立药学院的筹备工作取得进展，土地已落实，负责筹建工作的委员会也已完成考察。他说，下一步将包括校区设计和启动采购。马哈马总统还承诺支持该地区的其他教育基础设施需求，包括为安洛—阿菲亚德尼格巴高级中学新建宿舍楼，为希梅和安洛高级中学规划E栋教学楼，以及改善阿蒂亚维高级中学和技术学校的设施。他还回应了将奥豪沃农业学院升级为大学的呼声。在住房方面，总统表示，政府已为地区住房项目追加拨款GH¢500 million，并保证安洛民众将从中受益。他说，安洛加24小时营业市场项目正按计划推进，拟建的阿弗劳阿希加梅市场也已完成前期准备，土地已经落实，设计已经完成。据他介绍，由中国政府赠款资助的中国技术团队预计将前往项目现场核实设计，随后将拨付US$30 million赠款以启动项目。马哈马总统敦促沃尔塔地区协调委员会密切监督各项项目的实施，以确保项目如期交付

Unlock these with Subscription An ancient mound in Bihar's East Champaran district has been declared an archaeological site of national importance through a central government notification. The site – Ranivas Mound, at Kesariya – is spread over 1.63 acres and is under the ownership of the Bihar government, reads the gazette notification dated November 4 that was issued by the Ministry of Culture. Copies of the said notification were made available to the public on June 8, 2026 and "no objection has been received" from any person with regard to the declaration by the central government, said the notification signed by Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) Director General Yadubir Singh Rawat. A copy of the notification was affixed at a conspicuous place as required under sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958. A total of 3,686 sites around the country are under the care of the ASI, the Centre had informed Parliament in February 2026. A recommendation for listing the ancient Ranivas mound in Bihar as a centrally protected monument was sent to ASI headquarters in Delhi in 2021, a senior official told PTI in September 2022. According to the existing procedure, proposals or recommendations sent by regional ASI circles are examined by a team at the organisation’s headquarters before a final decision is taken on naming them monuments or sites of national importance. In case of meritorious proposals and recommendations, a provisional notification is first made, followed by the issuance of a final gazetted notification. A senior official said the inclusion of new sites under the ambit of the ASI is an ongoing process, based on recommendations received from various ASI “circles”, or regions, across the country from time to time. Centrally protected sites in Bihar fall under the jurisdiction of the ASI’s Patna Circle. Currently, 70 sites in Bihar are under the ambit of the ASI and governed by the Patna Circle, which is one of the oldest regional circles in India. The Patna Circle was earlier known as the Mid-Eastern Circle, and still earlier as the Buddhist Circle, ostensibly because of the important Buddhist monuments lying in the area, according to the Circle’s website. The ruins of the ancient Nalanda University in Bihar, also under the ASI, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The ancestral house of India’s first president Rajendra Prasad in Ziradei, Siwan, north Bihar, was officially declared a protected monument on May 27, 1991. Its provisional notification was done on October 30, 1990. The Shiva Temple in Gaya was notified by the ASI in 1996. Since then, no fresh site in Bihar had been brought under the ambit of the ASI, the senior official had said in September 2022. The Patna Circle earlier covered Jharkhand and a large number of sites in eastern Uttar Pradesh. While the Ranchi Circle was created in 2003 after Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar in 2000, a separate Sarnath Circle was created in 2013 for sites falling in eastern Uttar Pradesh. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/b.body_zh: 订阅账户还可享受 Premium Stories、Editorials、Opinions 等内容。订阅即可解锁这些内容。印度比哈尔邦东昌帕兰县的一座古土丘，经中央政府发布通知，已被宣布为国家重要考古遗址。文化和旅游部于11月4日发布的官方公报通知称，该遗址位于克萨里亚的拉尼瓦斯土丘，占地1.63英亩，归比哈尔邦政府所有。通知副本于2026年6月8日向社会公开，并由印度考古局（ASI）总监察长亚杜比尔·辛格·拉瓦特签署。通知称，中央政府作出这一宣布后，“未收到任何人的异议”。根据《1958年古迹与考古遗址及遗迹法》（AMASR Act, 1958）第4条第（1）款的规定，通知副本已张贴在显著位置。2026年2月，中央政府告知议会，全国共有3,686处遗址由印度考古局负责管理。2022年9月，一名高级官员告诉印度报业托拉斯（PTI），将比哈尔邦古老的拉尼瓦斯土丘列为中央保护古迹的建议，于2021年送交位于德里的印度考古局总部。按照现行程序，各地区印度考古局分局提交的提案或建议，均由该机构总部的团队审查，之后再就是否将其命名为国家重要古迹或遗址作出最终决定。对于有价值的提案和建议，首先会发布临时通知，随后发布正式的官方公报通知。一名高级官员称，将新遗址纳入印度考古局管理范围是一项持续进行的工作，依据的是该局各分局或地区不时提交的建议。印度考古局在比哈尔邦管理的中央保护遗址，隶属该局巴特那分局管辖。目前，比哈尔邦有70处遗址纳入印度考古局的管理范围，由巴特那分局负责监管；该分局是印度历史最悠久的地区分局之一。据该分局网站称，巴特那分局此前称为中东部分局，更早时称为佛教分局，表面上是因为该地区分布着重要的佛教古迹。同样由印度考古局管理的比哈尔邦古老那烂陀大学遗址，是联合国教科文组织世界遗产。印度首任总统拉金德拉·普拉萨德位于比哈尔邦北部锡万县齐拉代伊的祖居，于1991年5月27日正式宣布为受保护古迹，其临时通知于1990年10月30日发布。加亚的湿婆神庙于1996年被印度考古局列入通知名录。这名高级官员曾在2022年9月表示，自那以后，比哈尔邦没有新增遗址纳入印度考古局的管理范围。巴特那分局此前还负责贾坎德邦以及北方邦东部的大量遗址。2000年贾坎德邦从比哈尔邦分出后，兰契分局于2003年成立；2013年，又为北方邦东部境内的遗址成立了萨纳特分局。印度考古局成立于1861年，亚历山大·坎宁安担任该机构首任负责人。评论必须使用英文，并以完整句子表述。评论不得含有辱骂性内容或针对个人的攻击。请遵守我们的社区评论指南。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你已是《The Hindu》的注册用户并已登录，可以继续参与我们的文章互动。如果你还没有账户，请注册并登录后发表评论。用户登录自己的账户后，可以查看此前在 Vuukle 上发表的旧评论。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/npp-usa-elec.body: A member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP)’s United States branch, Opoku Boateng, has called for in-person voting and an immediate election timetable as the November 30 deadline for outstanding party polls approaches. In a statement, he raised concerns about what he described as inadequate communication from the committee overseeing the NPP-USA elections. According to Mr Boateng, members have yet to receive an election date, a published timetable or information on the register of eligible voters. “Members are not asking for miracles. They are asking for a timetable,” he said. He cited an October 29, 2026, directive by NPP General Secretary Justin Kodua requiring all outstanding elections to be completed by November 30. Mr Boateng argued that the lack of a clear roadmap was making it difficult for members to prepare and for candidates to organise their campaigns. The statement said the NPP-USA election was initially expected in July 2026 but was postponed after disagreements over an electronic voting system developed by NPP Ghana. According to Mr Boateng, members questioned the platform’s independence and raised concerns that it had not been tested in Ghana's elections. “It is important to understand that rejecting a particular voting platform does not mean rejecting democracy, technology, or the desire to elect leaders,” he said. As an alternative, he proposed voting at the various chapters, with results subsequently collated at the NPP-USA branch level. He also called for consideration of a regulated proxy voting arrangement for members unable to attend physically. He said this should include verification and accountability measures to prevent duplication, impersonation, and abuse. “The proposal is not intended to complicate the election. It is intended to build confidence,” he said. Mr Boateng also questioned how the electoral committee had been constituted. He alleged that the General Secretary established it directly, without the expected consultation with NPP-USA executives. He urged the committee to engage chapter leaders, executives, candidates and members to address concerns and build confidence in the process. His demands include publishing the voter register, allowing members to verify their eligibility and clarifying voting and results-collation procedures. He cautioned against waiting until the final days before the deadline to announce arrangements. “A credible election cannot be organised through last-minute announcements, hurried arrangements, and inadequate communication,” he said. While acknowledging the importance of meeting the deadline, Mr Boateng said speed should not come at the expense of fairness. He appealed to members to remain united despite differences over candidates and voting methods, saying the priority should be an election that strengthens the branch

Unlock these with Subscription Hundreds of students under the aegis of All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) staged a protest at Vivekananda Circle in Dharwad on Friday, condemning the State government’s move to allow adoption of government schools by private institutions and corporate companies. Addressing the protesters, AIDSO district secretary Shashikala Meti alleged that the Congress government, which had promised to protect government schools, was pursuing policies such as the Karnataka Public Schools (KPS)-Magnet initiative and an agreement with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) that would undermine the public education system. She alleged that the government had held a meeting at Vidhana Soudha on November 4 to facilitate the handing over of government schools to private institutions and corporate companies, with 2,000 schools proposed to be taken up in the first phase. She termed the move a betrayal of the people. Ms. Meti also criticised Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and the government representatives for allegedly making derogatory remarks about government school teachers and blaming them for declining educational standards, while overlooking shortcomings in its own policies. She said the government was proposing that private institutions adopt three government schools each, with the provision to name the schools after the adopting institutions. Other proposals reportedly included deputing teachers from private schools and providing old buses, laboratory equipment and computers. The government should address deficiencies in public education and recruit adequate numbers of teachers instead of shifting its responsibility to private entities, she said. Ms. Meti alleged that 14 government schools had already been merged with the KPS at Hegganuru in Kanakapura, Bengaluru South district, contradicting the government’s assurance that no government school would be closed. She demanded the immediate withdrawal of the government’s education policies and called upon the public to join a movement against what she termed the “corporate takeover” of public education. AIDSO district president Sindhu Kou di, district organisers Shantesh Nandikollam, Siddalingappa Chippalakatti and Ravishankar Poladi, among others took part in the protest. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: A senior North Korean ruling party official has met his counterpart in Beijing, the North's state media said Saturday, the latest in a series of high-level meetings during his visit this week. Kim Song-nam, a Political Bureau member and Central Committee secretary of North Korea's Workers' Party of Korea (WPA), met Liu Haixing, head of the Communist Party of China's (CPC) Central Committee's International Liaison Department, at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse on Friday, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said. It was Kim's third meeting with a senior Chinese official since he arrived Tuesday, as the two countries are seeking to deepen ties and expand cooperation after Chinese President Xi Jinping's June summit with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in Pyongyang. Kim briefed Liu on Pyongyang's "successes" in party-building work and said the whole country has been striving to meet the targets of the five-year plan adopted at the party's ninth congress in February. For his part, Liu called the visit significant for strengthening relations, according to the report. The two sides reaffirmed support for each other's policies and pledged deeper cooperation. Following the meeting, China hosted a reception for the North Korean delegation. In a separate dispatch, the KCNA said Kim also met Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau and director of its General Office, on Friday. At the meeting, Kim reaffirmed Pyongyang's commitment to closer ties. Kim began his high-level meetings Thursday with Foreign Minister Wang Yi. His delegation arrived in Beijing as the two countries seek to shore up cooperation after relations appeared to cool amid North Korea's deepening alignment with Russia over the war in Ukraine

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body_zh: 据朝鲜官方媒体周六报道，朝鲜执政党一名高级官员在北京会见了中方对口官员，这是他本周访问期间一系列高层会晤中的最新一次。朝鲜劳动党中央政治局委员兼中央委员会书记金松南周五在钓鱼台国宾馆会见了中共中央对外联络部部长刘海星，朝鲜中央通讯社报道称。这是金松南自周二抵达以来第三次会见中国高级官员，当时两国正寻求在今年6月中国国家主席习近平与朝鲜领导人金正恩在平壤举行峰会后深化关系并扩大合作。金松南向刘海星介绍了平壤在党建工作方面取得的“成就”，并表示全国上下都在努力实现党第九次代表大会2月通过的五年计划目标。刘海星则表示此次访问对加强两国关系具有重要意义，双方重申支持彼此的政策并承诺深化合作。会晤结束后，中方为朝鲜代表团举行了招待会。朝鲜中央通讯社在另一篇报道中称，金松南周五还与中共中央政治局常委、中央办公厅主任蔡奇举行了会晤。会晤中，金松南重申了平壤致力于加强两国关系的承诺。金松南于周四开始高层会晤，首先会见了外交部长王毅。他的代表团抵达北京之际，两国正寻求加强合作，此前因朝鲜在乌克兰战争中与俄罗斯加深结盟而使双边关系显得有所冷却。

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: NEW YORK — AI stocks are bouncing back Friday and recovering some of their sell-off from the last two days. The rest of the U.S. stock market is mixed following a whirlwind few days of Wall Street trying to sort out what this week’s sweeping victories by Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections will mean for the economy. The S&P 500 rose 0.9 percent and trimmed its loss for the week to 2.1 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 3 points, or less than 0.1 percent, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 1.6 percent higher. Even with this week's extreme swings, the S&P 500 remains only 5.1 percent below its all-time high, which was set last month. It and other companies tied to the build-out of AI data centers tumbled this week on worries that Democratic victories in statehouses across the country could mean a slowdown in further construction, particularly in Texas. Voters across political parties say they’re wary about AI and don’t like increases to power bills caused by data centers. That built on top of worries already rattling the industry that further construction of AI data centers may slow because of how expensive it’s become to borrow money. Before that, even, critics were saying AI stock prices had shot too high and were in a bubble. But political power in Washington will still be split between a Democratic Congress and a White House run by the Republican Trump, who retains the power to veto. That could limit federal efforts to rein in the AI industry. In the meantime, companies in the industry still see strong growth. IREN, a company that delivers data centers, compute and software for AI training, reported stronger results for the latest quarter than analysts expected. Its stock jumped 19.5 percent, and it also announced two new contracts signed since the end of the quarter. “We own the land, the power and the data centers under all of it, which gives us more ways to fund growth and lets us set its pace,” co-CEO Daniel Roberts said. Lam Research, a company whose equipment and services help make semiconductors, climbed 9.9 percent after announcing a program to send up to $25 billion to its investors by buying back shares of its own stock. That helped other stocks that have benefited from the build-out of AI data centers recover some of their own sharp losses. CoreWeave, which rents out access to AI chips to customers over the cloud, rose 4.5 percent. Micron Technology, which sells memory for computers, climbed 5.9 percent. Outside of AI, the U.S. stock market was mixed, and slightly more stocks fell within the S&P 500 than rose. Axon Enterprise tumbled 17.6 percent after the seller of Tasers reported weaker results for the latest quarter than analysts expected. It also announced a $1.2 billion investment in Skydio, a drone technology company. Charter Communications sank 5 percent after the internet and video provider reported a loss for the latest quarter, when analysts were expecting a profit. In the bond market, Treasury yields recovered some of their sharp drops from earlier in the week, triggered by tumbling stock prices and hopes that split control of Washington could limit how much more the U.S. government adds to its debt. The yield on the 10-year Treasury edged up to 4.85 percent from 4.84 percent late Thursday. It had topped 5.30 percent last month when worries about inflation, higher interest rates and rising government debt were spiking. Helping to support yields was a report showing U.S. employers hired many more workers last month than economists expected. It’s the latest signal that the U.S. economy continues to chug along despite high inflation. On one hand, the encouraging data could mean the U.S. economy may be able to absorb a slowdown in construction of AI data centers. But at the same time, the strong growth in jobs could push upward on inflation. Following the report, traders saw a greater probability of the Federal Reserve hiking its short-term interest rate at its next meeting in December, according to data from CME Group. Rate hikes by the Fed can rein in inflation, but they do so by making borrowing money more expensive for everyone and slowing the overall economy. A separate report, meanwhile, suggested that sentiment among U.S. consumers unexpectedly improved. The preliminary report from the University of Michigan said sentiment rose for lower- and middle-wealth Americans but fell for those with the largest stock portfolios. Perhaps more importantly for the bond market, the survey also suggested expectations for inflation in the coming year eased for Americans. That could prevent a vicious cycle where expectations for high inflation drive behavior that only worsens inflation
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 人工智能概念股遭全球抛售，华尔街本周跌幅收窄
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 纽约消息——人工智能股票周五反弹，收复了过去两天抛售的部分跌幅。在华尔街经历了一连串跌宕起伏、试图判断本周民主党在美国中期选举中取得广泛胜利将如何影响经济之后，美国股市其余板块涨跌互现。标普500指数上涨0.9%，全周跌幅收窄至2.1%。截至东部时间上午11时45分，道琼斯工业平均指数下跌3点，跌幅不足0.1%；纳斯达克综合指数上涨1.6%。尽管本周行情剧烈波动，标普500指数仍仅比上月创下的历史高点低5.1%。该指数成分股及其他与人工智能数据中心建设相关的公司本周重挫，原因包括担心民主党在全国各州议会获胜可能意味着进一步建设放缓，尤其是在得克萨斯州。各政治派别的选民表示，他们对人工智能持谨慎态度，也不喜欢数据中心推高电费。这一因素又叠加了已经令该行业不安的担忧：由于借贷成本大幅上升，人工智能数据中心的进一步建设可能放缓。此前，甚至已有批评者称人工智能股票价格涨得过高，存在泡沫。不过，华盛顿的政治权力仍将由民主党控制的国会和共和党人特朗普掌控的白宫分享，特朗普仍保留否决权。这可能限制联邦政府监管人工智能行业的努力。与此同时，该行业公司仍预计将实现强劲增长。IREN是一家提供人工智能训练所需数据中心、算力和软件的公司，其最新季度业绩好于分析师预期。该公司股价上涨19.5%，并宣布在季度结束后又签署了两份新合同。联席首席执行官丹尼尔·罗伯茨说：“我们拥有土地、电力以及贯穿其中的数据中心，这使我们有更多方式为增长提供资金，也能自行掌控增长速度。”半导体制造设备和服务企业Lam Research宣布一项计划，通过回购自身股票向投资者返还最多250亿美元后，股价上涨9.9%。这也帮助其他受益于人工智能数据中心建设的股票收复了部分大幅跌幅。CoreWeave通过云端向客户提供人工智能芯片使用服务，股价上涨4.5%。销售计算机存储芯片的美光科技上涨5.9%。人工智能板块之外，美国股市涨跌互现，标普500指数成分股中下跌股票略多于上涨股票。Taser制造商Axon Enterprise最新季度业绩不及分析师预期，股价暴跌17.6%。该公司还宣布向无人机技术企业Skydio投资12亿美元。互联网和视频服务提供商Charter Communications最新季度出现亏损，而分析师原本预计其将实现盈利，股价下跌5%。债券市场上，美国国债收益率从本周早些时候的急跌中有所回升；此前股市暴跌，加之市场希望华盛顿的分裂格局能够限制美国政府进一步增加债务，均对收益率走势产生影响。10年期美国国债收益率从周四晚间的4.84%小幅升至4.85%。上月，在通胀、利率上升和政府债务攀升的担忧推动下，该收益率一度突破5.30%。一份报告显示，美国雇主上月招聘的 workers数量远多于经济学家预期，为收益率提供支撑。这是尽管通胀高企，美国经济仍在缓慢运行的最新迹象。一方面，这一令人鼓舞的数据可能意味着美国经济能够承受人工智能数据中心建设放缓；但另一方面，就业的强劲增长可能推高通胀。报告发布后，根据CME Group的数据，交易员认为美联储在12月下一次会议上上调短期利率的可能性更大。美联储加息能够抑制通胀，但方式是提高所有人的借贷成本，并拖累整体经济。与此同时，另一份报告显示，美国消费者信心意外改善。密歇根大学的初步报告称，中低收入和中等财富美国人的信心上升，但股票投资组合规模最大的群体信心下降Perhaps对债券市场而言更重要的是，调查还显示，美国人对未来一年通胀的预期有所缓和。这可能避免形成恶性循环：高通胀预期驱动相关行为，而这些行为只会进一步加剧通胀

Unlock these with Subscription Mysuru has figured in the list of cities adjudged for the Swachh Survekshan-2025-26 awards, with the Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) receiving a formal invitation from the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to attend the award presentation ceremony scheduled to be held in New Delhi on November 11. The invitation marks Mysuru’s inclusion in the national-level recognition for urban cleanliness and sanitation. The prestigious Swachh Survekshan-2026 awards would be presented by President Droupadi Murmu at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi. However, there is no official information yet on the category in which Mysuru has been selected for an award or the rank it has secured. The details will be known only after the rankings and award categories are officially announced. In 2024-25, Mysuru was ranked 3rd cleanest city in India in the 3 to 10 lakh population category under Super Swachh League (SSL), which was a newly introduced category. Mysuru was ranked the cleanest city in India for two consecutive years – 2015 and 2016. MCC Commissioner M.K. Savita and a team of officers are visiting New Delhi for the award function. Minister in-charge of Mysuru district and Urban Development Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah and senior officials were also expected to attend the function, sources in MCC said. Expressing happiness over the invitation, Ms. Savitha credited Mysuru’s cleanliness initiatives over the years to the collective efforts of former commissioners, health officials, pourakarmikas, and engineers, who, had worked together as a team to address the shortcomings identified in earlier surveys to bring recognition to the city. The MCC Commissioner said that the 11th edition of Swachh Survekshan had commenced and expressed hope that Mysuru would secure a good position in the 2026-27 survey as well. The 10th edition of Swachh Survekshan-2025-26 was conducted under the theme ‘Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel – Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath’. Mysuru MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar expressed happiness over the MCC being invited to the Swachh Survekshan award function and congratulated pourakarmikas and citizens for their efforts. “Let us all work together to further enhance Mysuru’s reputation on the cleanliness front,” he added. “This is a proud moment for the State. Official announcement of the ranking is awaited. I congratulate the pourakarmikas, MCC officials, staff and citizens of Mysuru ahead of the award presentation,” said the Urban Development Minister, in a statement.
